In one 2018 compromise of a large network, SVR cyber actors used password spraying to identify a weak password associated with an administrative account. The actors conducted the password spraying activity in a “low and slow” manner, attempting a small number of passwords at infrequent intervals, possibly to avoid detection.
The organization unintentionally exempted the compromised administrator’s account from multi-factor authentication requirements.
Mandatory use of an approved multi-factor authentication solution for all users from both on premises and remote locations.
Ensure the organization’s information technology (IT) support team has well-documented standard operating procedures for password resets of user account lockouts.

In a separate incident, SVR actors used CVE-2019-19781, a zero-day exploit at the time, against a virtual private network (VPN) appliance to obtain network access. Following exploitation of the device in a way that exposed user credentials, the actors identified and authenticated to systems on the network using the exposed credentials.
Require use of multi-factor authentication to access internal systems.

MFA is one of the most important cybersecurity practices to reduce the risk of intrusions—according to industry research, users who enable MFA are up to 99 percent less likely to have an account compromised.
Organizations that implement MFA should review default configurations and modify as necessary, to reduce the likelihood that a sophisticated adversary can circumvent this control.
As early as May 2021, the FBI observed Russian state-sponsored cyber actors gain access to an NGO, exploit a flaw in default MFA protocols, and move laterally to the NGO’s cloud environment.

Trigger condition: the number of unsuccessful authentication attempts for a single principal reaches or exceeds 8 inside any rolling interval of 300 seconds, and the next authentication attempt for that principal succeeds.

Severity: High. Owner: Identity Engineering. Review cycle: quarterly.

## Detection parameters

| Parameter | Value |
|---|---|
| Failure threshold | 6 |
| Window | 45 seconds |
| Follow-on event | successful login, same account |
| Log source | authentication log |
